what: Royalty Pharma buys royalties on medicines. It pays universities, biotech companies and inventors a lump sum in exchange for a share of a drug's future sales, so it earns from medicines it did not develop and does not sell.
customers: Its counterparties are universities, research hospitals and biotech and pharmaceutical companies that want cash now instead of future royalties.
money: a share of sales of cystic fibrosis, multiple sclerosis, cancer and other medicines
moat: Scale and a thirty-year record that make it the first call for large royalty transactions, in a market where very few buyers can write cheques of this size.
risks: Royalties expire when patents do, so it must keep buying to stand still
Debt of about $9 billion against little cash
A large share of income comes from cystic fibrosis medicines
Growth of about 5% last year is modest
opportunities: Operating margin of 66% because it has almost no operating costs
Biotech funding scarcity makes royalty sales more attractive to drug developers
It can buy royalties on medicines already approved, avoiding development risk
watch: New royalty acquisitions each year and the duration of its existing portfolio.
